newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up on improved sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up on improved sentiment.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed higher on Wednesday in volume trade on firm sentiment, brokers said.
The all-share index closed up 3.68 points at 648.38. Price gains led declines by 37 to nine. Commercial Bank rose five rupees to 165, Walkers Tours 2.75 to 18.25.
"There is optimism in the air after the opposition said it had ratified an agreement with the government to adopt a common front to the ethnic crisis," said a John Keells trader.
Turnover was 107 million rupees on 1.7 million shares led by foreign buying of 300,000 shares of the blue chip Development Finance Corporation of Ceylon.
Foreign buying was 77.2 million rupees and selling 19.4 million.
"It is becoming possible to execute big trades because sellers are starting to loosen up more with every point the all-share gains," said a broker at Jardine Fleming.
Sellers were holding back hoping to get higher prices when first quarter 1997 results come out in May, brokers said.
Corporate growth in 1997 is expected to be good because of better power situation than in 1996 and low-cost corporate borrowings after the Central Bank cut reserve ratios.
The Bank cut the ratios of commercial banks by three percent this yea, in a bid to reduce cost of corporate borrowings.
